rationale:
Evidence: the best-scored design so far is iteration 2 (score 65.2489, 60 trials, 0 finishes). Every track ends off track. Max error is 0.0677 (oval), 0.0614 (s-bend) and 0.0645 (slalom), so all three exceed the 0.06 m limit. rms_error is 0.024 to 0.028 m, so the failures are in peak excursions. Progress is 0.25 (oval), 0.13 (s-bend) and 0.10 (slalom).

Review of the round-2 critique. I accept three points. (1) My iteration-2 claim that max_error 'did not fall as kp rose from 5 to 7' was wrong. The three oval values come from designs that differ in several gains, so they cannot isolate kp, and I withdraw that conclusion. (2) My reasoning on kd was muddled. I cannot show from the data that raising kd helps or hurts, so I keep kd at 0.3 and do not test it now. (3) Attribution matters more than effect size. Changing ki alone from the best design is the only way to tell whether ki moves max_error. I keep the single-variable test.

I reject the critique's suggestion to add a second change now, such as a sensing fix or a speed change. Either would confound the ki result. The sensing gap (the line is seen only out to about 0.044 m offset) is real, but it needs a geometry change, which I will test in a separate race. Completion is the largest score term, and no run has finished, so completion_time is requested to show whether runs are slow or stopped. I cannot yet say which, so I set no speed change in this race.

Change: ki 0.1 to 0.2, with everything else identical to iteration 2 (kp 7.0, kd 0.3, base_speed 1.4, last_direction, same geometry). The integral is capped at +/-2, so the maximum integral contribution is 0.4 turn, about 140 PWM counts. The critique is right that the slalom signal alternates sign, so the integral can oscillate there. The slalom is therefore a kill check.

Hypotheses: max_error falls to 0.06 m or below on the oval and s-bend. line_loss_events fall to 1 or fewer per run on the oval. Oval progress rises above 0.27. These are predictions, not derived values.

Kill and follow-up rules, using one threshold of 30 percent for steering_oscillation as in the earlier round: if steering_oscillation rises by more than 30 percent, or slalom progress falls below 0.10, ki returns to 0.1. If max_error is still above 0.06 m on all tracks, the next single test is the sensing fix, not a higher ki. If completion_time exceeds 3 s on runs that stay on track, the next single test is base_speed plus 0.1.
